description: Set a JVM (Java or Kotlin) project's version to an exact value, for Maven or Gradle builds. Maven — for a single-module `pom.xml`, rewrites the root artifact's own `<version>` element in place (the first `<version>` that is a direct child of `<project>`, never the `<parent>`'s version or a dependency/plugin's version); for a Maven reactor (the root `pom.xml` declares `<modules>`), instead runs `mvn versions:set -DnewVersion=<new-version> -DgenerateBackupPoms=false` so every module and parent reference updates consistently in one step. Gradle (Kotlin DSL or Groovy, wrapper preferred — e.g. a Kotlin Spring Boot or Quarkus service, or a plain JVM library) — finds every place the project version is declared as a literal (`version=` in `gradle.properties`, `version = "…"` / `version '…'` in any module's `build.gradle(.kts)`, a `gradle.properties` key or `gradle/libs.versions.toml` `[versions]` entry the build script reads it from), refuses to write when modules disagree until the user confirms, and rewrites them all to the new value. Android Gradle projects are out of scope — see `iru-android-bump-version`. Invoke as `/iru-java-bump-version <new-version>` where `<new-version>` is the literal target version (e.g. `1.4.0` or `1.4.1-SNAPSHOT`) — this skill does not compute bumps itself, it only applies the value it's given (`iru-release` computes the release/next-dev values per the pre-release convention documented in this file and passes each one through in turn). Also accepts `args`: `sync-files: yes|no` (default: ask) to also update README/Antora version mentions, `next-version: <upcoming-version>` so that sync maps "Latest release" markers to `<new-version>` and "Latest snapshot"/"Current development version" markers to the upcoming pre-release value instead of rewriting every marker to the single value, and `dry-run: yes|no` (default `no`) to print the diff/command without writing or running anything. Reports the old and new version, the build tool and whether the project was treated as a reactor/multi-module build or a single module, and every file touched. Use whenever the user, or another skill such as `iru-release`, needs a Maven or Gradle JVM project's version set to a specific value instead of hand-editing `pom.xml` or Gradle build files.
